title: Lucena: building the bridge
outcomes: Explains in plain words how the attacker wins with a pawn on the seventh when the king stands in front of it and the enemy king is cut off
Avoids two tempting errors in the Lucena position: promoting at once and blocking a check with a loose rook
Tells a Lucena-type win from the same arrangement that only draws, and names the feature that changed

steps.text: **Lucena.** The pawn is on the seventh rank and your king stands in front of it, on the queening square, so the pawn cannot move. The enemy king is cut off: your rook holds a file it may not cross. If your king steps aside, the enemy rook starts checking. You win by moving the king out and sheltering it behind your own rook. It is a plan with conditions, not a reflex.

steps.caption: Lucena-type: White to move wins. One winning line is shown.

line.say: A rook check pushes Black's king away.
The rook goes to the fourth rank, ready to block checks there.
White's king steps out of the queening square.
Black's rook checks along the f-file.
The king steps off the file.
Black's rook checks again, now along the e-file.
The king steps toward the rook.
The king steps up the board, next to the fourth rank.
Black checks along the e-file again.
The rook blocks on e4 and the king defends it, so Black's rook cannot take it with a win. This shelter is the bridge.

claims.statement: White wins from the start position.

steps.text: **Conditions.** Lucena needs a pawn on the seventh, your king in front of it and the enemy king cut off. Two moves often spoil it: promoting while the enemy rook can take the new queen, and blocking a check with a loose rook (one your king does not defend). The bridge is a block by your own rook, on a square your king defends. Before you count on the win, ask what else about the arrangement matters.

steps.title: Same arrangement, one file apart
steps.prompt: Both positions have the pawn on the seventh, the king in front of it and the enemy king cut off. In one the pawn is on a central file, in the other on the edge file. Which one wins? Predict, then check.
In which position did you want to promote or to check at once? What did you not look at before you moved: the rook's safety, or what the other rook could take?
